correctness.rationale: An independent fibre argument gives the index. After the coordinate sign change x_i=(-1)^i h_i, the homogeneous equation is the t-th forward difference equation. Its bilateral solutions are exactly h_i=Σ_{0≤j<t} c_j binom(i,j): Pascal's identity gives solutions, initial forward differences determine the first t values by a unit triangular system, and the recurrence has unit endpoint coefficients in both directions. The possible pair differences h_d−h_0 form exactly the ideal generated by binom(d,j), 1≤j<t, while h_0 is unrestricted. Because the output map is onto, output fibres are translates of this kernel. In the original coordinates the pair invariant is consequently x_d−(−1)^d x_0 modulo that ideal. For 1≤j≤p^a, the identity binom(d,j)=(d/j)binom(d−1,j−1) gives valuation a−ν_p(j), since ν_p(d−h)=ν_p(h) for 1≤h<j. The least valuation is a−floor(log_p(t−1)) for 2≤t≤p^a, zero once the term j=p^a is included, and the empty ideal at t=1 gives e=r. This includes p∤d and d=1. In the (z+1) basis the remainder of integer division has coefficients divisible by p^e, so its monic quotient gives the claimed finite decoder; its level sets have index p^e, matching the fibre argument. Haar pushforwards give uniform mass on each image coset conditionally and full Haar unconditionally, for relative density p^e on the chosen coset and mutual information e log p. The finite polynomial and kernel checks are supportive only; no uploaded code was run.
residual_risks: The proof does not cover periodic spatial rings or non-Haar input laws; indices here are compact-group indices, not counts of individual configurations.
